sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Chatham County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Two separate offices handle a Chatham County property tax bill. The Board of Assessors sets the value and approves exemptions, while the Tax Commissioner bills, collects and passes the money to each taxing body. The Tax Commissioner states that its office plays no part in setting values or millage rates.

According to the county's 2026 property tax brochure, the Tax Commissioner bills for Chatham County, the Special Service District, the school board, transit, Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Thunderbolt, Tybee Island and Vernonburg. Look at the line items on your own bill to see which of those districts apply to your address.

  • Tax Commissioner: 912-652-7100, tax.chathamcountyga.gov, 222 W. Oglethorpe Ave., 295 Police Memorial Dr. and 1145 Eisenhower Dr., open 8:30am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday.
  • Board of Assessors: 912-652-7271, boa.chathamcountyga.gov, Suite 113 of the Pete Liakakis Government Building at 222 West Oglethorpe Avenue.
  • Mail: Chatham County Tax Commissioner, P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412.
  • Satellite tax offices on Wilmington Island Road, US 80 and Georgia Highway 21 see people by appointment only.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Chatham County itself?
sections.html:
Chatham County is the northernmost of Georgia's coastal counties. It covers 632 square miles, and 206 of them are water. The Savannah River bounds it on the northeast and the Ogeechee River on the southwest and Tybee Island sits on the Atlantic side. Savannah is the county seat, and the other municipalities are Bloomingdale, Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Tybee Island, Thunderbolt and Vernonburg.

The Census Bureau estimated 311,855 residents in July 2025, up from 295,291 at the 2020 count. QuickFacts lists a 2020 to 2024 median owner-occupied home value of $302,700, a median gross rent of $1,471 and an owner-occupancy rate of 56.8%. It also shows 4,426 building permits issued in 2025.

Interstates 16, 95 and 516 cross the county along with US 17 and US 80, and the whole county falls inside Savannah-Chatham County Public Schools. Savannah State University and the Savannah College of Art and Design are both located in Savannah, and Live Oak Public Libraries serve Chatham, Effingham and Liberty counties.

sections.h2: When are Chatham County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real property is billed in two installments each year, due June 1 and November 15. Personal property is billed once, with the whole amount due by November 15.

Chatham County billing calendar, from the Tax Commissioner's 2026 property tax brochure
BillMailed byDue
Real property, first installmentApril 1June 1
Real property, second installmentSeptember 15November 15
Personal property, one billNot statedNovember 15

Payment can go by mail to the Chatham County Tax Commissioner at P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412, online, or in person. Online payment by credit card or eCheck carries convenience fees, and the brochure says eChecks are free. A check or eCheck that comes back unpaid costs 5% of the amount with a $30 minimum, under O.C.G.A. 16-9-20.

Taxes not paid by the due date are delinquent. Interest and penalties follow O.C.G.A. 48-2-40 and 48-2-44, and a delinquent parcel can also carry a tax lien that a title company will want cleared before closing.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Chatham County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date printed on your Annual Notice of Assessment to appeal in writing to the Board of Assessors. The notice, not a tax bill, starts that clock. An appeal can argue taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and Georgia supplies a uniform appeal form.

On that first written appeal you must name your method. The brochure lists three:

  • Board of Equalization, with a further petition to Superior Court.
  • Arbitration, which requires a certified appraisal submitted within 45 days; the Board of Assessors can accept or reject it, and you may still petition Superior Court.
  • Hearing Officer, open only to non-homestead real property with a fair market value of $500,000 or more, or certain wireless property above $200,000 in total value.

The Board of Assessors says it welcomes recent sales, photographs of similar sold homes, and lease or income figures. It also points out that it measures square footage from the outside perimeter, so a smaller interior living area does not by itself prove an error.

Returns for real and personal property are filed between January 1 and April 1, and the forms are on the Board of Assessors website under Forms. Once an initial return is on file it renews automatically at the value last finally set. Filing a new return with a different declared value during that window is also how a taxpayer who disagrees with the current value preserves appeal rights if the Board changes the value again. Agricultural land used for bona fide farming can be assessed at 30% rather than 40% of fair market value, and conservation use property is valued at its current use, but both programs require a covenant to keep the property in that use for at least 10 years.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can Chatham County homeowners claim?
sections.html:
The regular homestead exemption takes $12,000 off the assessed value for county taxes and $2,000 off for school and state taxes. To claim any homestead exemption you must own, occupy and claim the home as your legal residence on January 1, and rental property does not qualify.

  • Stephens-Day and the state floating homestead exemption: the county awards whichever gives the larger saving, then adds other exemptions you qualify for.
  • Special Chatham senior exemption: age 65 by January 1, combined net income of $10,000 or less, $30,000 off county and school assessed value plus relief from most state assessments.
  • Senior school exemption: age 62, combined net income of $25,000 or less.
  • Disabled veteran exemption: a VA letter showing 100% service-connected disability, with the amount subject to annual change.
  • Year's Support: a surviving spouse or minor child who petitions Probate Court within two years of a death can obtain property tax relief for the year named in the petition.

Bring a Georgia driver's license or ID and a vehicle registration in your name, with matching mailing and homestead addresses. Applications received within 45 days of the notice date count for the current year, and a later filing is considered for the next year. A new application is needed after buying a new home or changing the deed.

sections.h2: What happens to my Chatham County tax bill if I sell?
sections.html:
The seller is billed because Georgia taxes whoever owned the property on January 1. A sale in March or August does not move the bill to the buyer, and the Department of Revenue says state law allows no refund of tax for part of a year.

That makes proration a private deal between buyer and seller at closing. A sale between the June 1 and November 15 due dates leaves the second installment open, so ask the closing attorney whether it is being paid at the table or credited to the buyer. A delinquent balance should be paid from proceeds so the lien does not follow the title.

Your homestead exemption stays with the person who applied, so the new owner files again. If you inherited the house, remember the Year's Support option described above, and call the Tax Commissioner at 912-652-7100 for a payoff figure before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Is Chatham County property tax paid once or twice a year?
faqs.a: Twice for real property. The first installment is due June 1 and the second November 15, with personal property due in full on November 15.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Chatham County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Board of Assessors at 912-652-7271. The Tax Commissioner at 912-652-7100 handles payments and cannot change a value or a millage rate.

faqs.q: Can I appeal after the 45 days pass?
faqs.a: Generally no. The deadline runs from the date printed on the assessment notice, and the Board of Assessors can tell you whether anything applies to a notice that never reached you.

faqs.q: Does a homestead exemption transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. The exemption belongs to the owner who applied, and the buyer must file a new application. Filing is done at the Board of Assessors with a Georgia license and matching vehicle registration.

faqs.q: Will I owe tax if I sell a Chatham County house in the fall?
faqs.a: You owe the bill for the year because you owned it on January 1. If the November 15 installment is still open at closing, the payoff or proration is settled on the closing statement.
